title: Pilot Harness Framework (shared infrastructure for all pilot-first directives)
purpose: Formalize the pilot-first pattern that saved us during canonical-name research. Provide a reusable harness so every new enrichment module, T1 agent, or external integration can run a bounded validation against hand-picked candidates before committing to production infrastructure. Meta-directive — produces tooling used by other directives, not a user-facing capability.
pilot_rationale: This IS the pilot infrastructure. Not meta-piloting it.

exported_functions.name: run_pilot
exported_functions.signature: run_pilot(directive_id: str, candidates: list[dict], ground_truth: dict, under_test_fn: Callable) -> PilotResult
exported_functions.description: Run under_test_fn against each candidate. Compare output to ground_truth. Compute precision/recall/runtime stats. Return PilotResult with verdict (PASS/FAIL/ABORT) and evidence JSON.

exported_functions.name: write_pilot_report
exported_functions.description: Write structured pilot report to /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/fixes/pilot_{directive_id}_results.json for operator review.

exported_functions.name: gate_production_deploy
exported_functions.description: Return True only if pilot meets all thresholds (precision, recall, runtime, abort_conditions none triggered). If False, caller must not proceed to production deploy.

pilot_result_schema.operator_notes_required: bool (true if any abort or FAIL)

conventions: Pilot candidates must be human-selected, not randomly sampled
Ground truth must be provided by a human BEFORE the pilot runs (pre-registered, not retrofitted)
Pilot results are append-only — never overwrite a previous pilot run, always new timestamp
A failing pilot is data, not a crisis — it means the approach needs rethinking, not that the module is buggy
Pilot success does NOT imply production readiness — it means 'approach is viable, now build the real module'. Operator review still required.
why_this_matters: Canonical-naming pilot (15 candidates, 15/15 bridges found) told us ecosyste.ms was viable BEFORE we built the fetcher daemon. That's 4 hours saved vs building and then discovering the data source didn't work.
Signal_bridge bug (created_at vs computed_at typo) silently returned 0 bridges for 24 hours. A ground-truth pilot (expected: ~100 bridges) would have caught it immediately.
Adapter run_id NOT NULL bug produced 100% write failures. Ground-truth pilot with expected-writes >0 would have failed loudly instead of returning success.
The pattern of 'hand-pick candidates, pre-register expectations, measure' is how every scientific discipline validates instruments. We should adopt it for every external-data-source integration.

integration_with_existing_gates.note: Pilot harness is upstream of Gate 8 (circuit breaker) and Gate 9 (signal variance). Pilot catches issues before the enrichment starts running. Gates catch issues after it's running. Complementary, not redundant.
